---
title: "Ensure robust to new data"
---

A fitted recipe is a model of the training data, applied to data it has
never seen. Some of the failure modes that come with that are handled for
you, and two are yours to prevent: missing values and category levels the
training data lacked.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Key points"}
* Discuss how training data is used to fit a pre-processing models that transform test data.
* Common failure modes when transforming test data.
* Things Recipes does for you
  - Apply normalization fit from training to test
  - Data leakage in general
* Things you should do w/ Recipes:
  - Missing values (impute)
  - Rare / Missing category levels
:::

## Setup

```{python}
import polars as pl
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

from shoez import Recipe, StepDummy, StepImputeMedian, StepNormalize, StepOther, StepUnknown
from shoez import Selectors as s
from shoez.data import ames_mini, credit

credit_train, credit_validation = train_test_split(
    credit, train_size=0.75, stratify=credit["Status"], random_state=1
)
ames_train, ames_validation = train_test_split(ames_mini, train_size=0.8, random_state=502)
```

## Training data fits, new data is transformed

Everything a recipe estimates comes from the frame passed to `fit()`, and
`transform()` reuses those estimates on every other frame. That is the
guard against data leakage: the validation set never influences the
statistics that transform it. After normalizing with the training means, the
validation mean is close to zero but not exactly zero.

```{python}
recipe = (
    Recipe(data=credit_train, target="Status")
    .add(StepImputeMedian(s.numeric_features()))
    .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_features()))
)
fitted = recipe.fit(credit_train)
fitted.transform(credit_validation).select(pl.col("Income").mean())
```

The same holds for every step: the medians used to fill gaps, the levels a
dummy step expands, and the axes a PCA step projects onto are all fixed at
fit time.

## Missing values: impute first

Steps do not fill missing values for you. A normalize step passes nulls
through, a dummy step turns a null level into a row of null indicators, and
most models refuse either. Put `StepImputeMedian` (or `StepImputeMean`) and
`StepUnknown` before anything else so the later steps see complete columns.

Without them, the transformed validation set still carries the gaps:

```{python}
recipe = (
    Recipe(data=credit_train, target="Status")
    .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_features()))
    .add(StepDummy(s.nominal_features()))
)
fitted = recipe.fit(credit_train)
fitted.transform(credit_validation).null_count()
```

With imputation first, and `StepUnknown` giving missing categoricals their
own `"unknown"` level, nothing is left for a model to trip on:

```{python}
recipe = (
    Recipe(data=credit_train, target="Status")
    .add(StepImputeMedian(s.numeric_features()))
    .add(StepUnknown(s.nominal_features()))
    .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_features()))
    .add(StepDummy(s.nominal_features()))
)
fitted = recipe.fit(credit_train)
fitted.transform(credit_validation).null_count()
```

## Rare and unseen category levels

A dummy step learns its levels at fit time, so a level that first appears in
new data gets a row of all-zero indicators, silently. `StepOther(columns,
threshold=...)` prevents that: it pools levels rarer than the threshold into
one `"other"` level when fitted, and sends any level it has never seen to
the same place when transforming. In this split, `"Stone"` exterior appears
only in the validation rows:

```{python}
recipe = (
    Recipe(data=ames_train, target="Sale_Price")
    .add(StepOther(s.col("Exterior_1st"), threshold=0.01))
    .add(StepDummy(s.col("Exterior_1st")))
)
fitted = recipe.fit(ames_train)
stone = ames_validation.filter(pl.col("Exterior_1st") == "Stone")
fitted.transform(stone).select(pl.col("^Exterior_1st_.*$"))
```

Both rows land in `Exterior_1st_other`, a column the model has seen, rather
than in no column at all. Rare levels pooled at fit time also stop a dummy
step from producing near-empty indicator columns for them.
